column3: The villages are called Gath’s daughters.
Dominion is expressed as his hand.
The Hebrew names horsemen and says David hamstrung the chariotry, leaving a hundred chariots. It does not explicitly name horses.
Garrisons supply an unstated object; the Arameans are called servants.
The men are called servants, and the shields are described as being on them.
The Hebrew explicitly says to inquire about his welfare; Hadadezer is called a man of wars with Tou.
The Ammonites are called sons of Ammon.
The Hebrew calls David’s sons “the first” and places them at the king’s hand.
